driver: A standard gives each of several districts a whole number of staff from a head count on a future date, and no record holds the head count. Each district counted its members on two past dates; between and after them every movement is reported twice and incompletely, once by the place it enters at that place's own capture rate and once by the place it leaves at that place's own. The capture rates are published nowhere and the twice-reported matrix fixes them only up to one common factor, which a single independent count of one year's entries pins; exits are caught far less than entries and are the residual of the account between the two counts; and the counterparties' tables end three years before the date, so the last years are seen only by the home side's own record, at a fraction measured on the years both report. Taking each district's own tables, the fuller of the two reports, or rates scaled to the best reporter closes every check the record offers and misplaces the head counts by more than a staff step.
driver_concrete: Orlava staffs seven consular districts at one officer for every 5,000 citizens or part of 5,000 resident on 1 January 2027. The hosts' registers catch 0.56 to 1.21 of the citizens arriving and 0.24 to 0.97 of those leaving; Orlava's own catches 0.72 of foreign arrivals (pinned by its 2021 census) and 0.36 of its emigrants; the partners' tables end with 2023. Core: 36,457; 48,181; 36,488; 32,891; 12,399; 22,690; 62,457 citizens and 8, 10, 8, 7, 3, 5, 13 officers (Skarholm, Brennia, Marovia, Tesmar, Kestria, Fenmark, Almera), where the hosts' tables carried to 2027 give 9, 9, 11, 9, 3, 6, 15.
stump: A careful but hurried analyst takes each host's arrivals table as the arrivals (Brennia, which records 56 per cent of them, is then an officer short), its departures table as the exits (Marovia, which records 24 per cent of them, is three officers over) and carries 2021 to 2023 through the three years no partner's table reaches (Tesmar, where exits rose by three quarters, is an officer over).
deep_chain: (1) both reports of every flow among the eight states on one schema for 2011 to 2023, Orlava's own register to 2026, each host's two census counts and its births and deaths of citizens; (2) Orlava's arrival share from its census's foreign citizens who lived abroad a year before, each partner's share of its own emigrants from its flow to Orlava, each host's arrival share from the other partners' citizens moving to it; (3) each host's exits of citizens between its two censuses as the residual of the account on corrected arrivals, and the share its departures table caught; (4) Fenmark's 2016 count reproduced and 2021 to 2023 held out; (5) the share of moves to each host and of exits from it that Orlava's register catches on the years both sides report, and 2024 to 2026 from it; (6) citizens per host on 1 January 2027, officers by the standard, and the citizens who left each host since its 2021 census
judgment: a recording share no state publishes, fixed by the matrix only up to a level that one census table pins; exits no table holds, taken from the account between two censuses; three years no partner covers, seen by the home register at a fraction

lineage.driver: Activity at each site is seen through a sensor that records every event of some units and none of others, and the units it never records are spread unevenly across sites, so the missing activity is not a fixed share of what the sensor saw: it is rebuilt as the never-recorded units based at each site times the activity per such unit that the fully counted sites show, while one seen-to-counted ratio moves the missing activity from the sites holding those units to the sites whose units are all recorded.

lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is a period total over units whose reports arrive late, where a missing report has two causes: the intermediary that files a whole batch was late, which says nothing about the unit, or the unit failed to report on its own, which marks a unit that has shrunk or closed; only a unit missing while its usual batch-mates arrived separates the two, and a closed unit's outcome shows only in a closure record months later, so only cohorts old enough for closures to have been recorded measure what a unit's own failure to report implies.
lineage.driver_concrete: Each county's December 2026 covered jobs are estimated from the unemployment insurance quarterly reports received by 15 February 2027; payroll agents file their clients' reports in one transmission and at year end several statewide bureaus' transmissions come late, while an employer missing when its usual transmission arrived has usually shed jobs or stopped trading, and a stopped employer shows only in an account inactivation two or three quarters later, so its December jobs are read from quarters old enough for inactivations to have landed.
lineage.stump: A competent solver conforms the reports, amendments and worksites, imputes each employer whose December report had not arrived as the field does (its September jobs moved by its county's reporting employers' change), treats an employer missing two quarters as ceased, sees that imputation back-test with a steady upward miss under 0.7 of a point on the closed quarters and files that no county fell 2.0 per cent; an employer missing while its usual transmission-mates arrived has usually shed jobs or stopped trading and keeps 0.29 of its September jobs on the quarters old enough for inactivations to have landed, which puts two counties past the line.
lineage.answer: Garrow and Ostrom qualify (December 2026 covered jobs 3.0 and 3.1 per cent below December 2025); the field's imputation designates no county

lineage.driver: A period total is estimated early from a census of unit reports, and the part not yet observed is completed component by component, each from its own evidence: units whose report is out are read by whether the intermediary batch they arrive in has come, and those missing alone are carried at what such units kept on periods old enough for their closures to be recorded; units in late batches are carried at the change of all units whose standing is visible this period, the missing-alone included, because this period's closure rate is several times the closed periods'; units liable but not yet on the register are counted from this period's early registrations and the closed periods' registration delays, at the late registrants' size; and each multi-site unit whose site report is out is split by each site's own seasonal change a year earlier. No one component gives the set of areas below the threshold.
lineage.driver_concrete: Each Franklin county's December 2026 covered jobs are estimated from the unemployment insurance files as they stood on 15 February 2027: 6,053 of 27,796 liable employers' reports are out, 3,992 of them in payroll agents' late year-end batches (three or more reports received in the same second) and 815 outstanding on their own (kept 0.29 of September jobs on resolved quarters); the housing downturn puts 7.9 per cent of construction jobs with employers outstanding on their own against under one per cent at earlier fourth-quarter cut-offs, so the late batches are carried at the change of every employer whose standing shows (about 590 fewer jobs than the reporters' change); about 590 employers liable for the quarter have no account yet (2,400 jobs, counted from the quarter's 309 registrations so far and the delays of earlier fourth quarters, at the late registrants' 4.3 jobs); and the 185 multi-county employers whose worksite report is out are split by each worksite's own December-on-September change a year earlier, which takes about 260 jobs out of Kittredge, 150 out of Talcott and 80 out of Sayre.
lineage.stump: The careful pass carries every outstanding report alike, at its reporting peers' change by supersector times the share of such employers that reported in the end at earlier fourth-quarter cut-offs (0.92), develops the unregistered employers, and splits multi-county employers by the latest worksite report: it designates Ostrom, leaves Garrow at minus 1.9 and Kittredge at minus 0.9, and puts five counties outside their ranges by 0.7 of a point or more. With the outstanding reports carried alike and the rest right the set is Kittredge and Ostrom or Kittredge; with the latest worksite split and the rest right, Garrow and Ostrom; the reports received alone designate all fourteen; September carried flat designates Ostrom.
lineage.answer: Certify Garrow, Kittredge and Ostrom (December 2026 covered jobs an estimated 3.0, 3.0 and 3.1 per cent below December 2025 on the records of 15 February 2027; Bray, the nearest other county, at minus 1.1; the state at plus 0.1)
